results.description: A hefty Summer 1993 edition of The Taxpayer. Topics discussed within include the most indebted states in the world, the privatisation of firefighters, federal loan forgiveness, the Export Development Corporation's loans to the Bank of China, grants dispensed by the federal Department of Energy, Mines, and Resources, grants dispensed by the federal Department of Industry, Science, and Technology, Saskatchewan's Crown corporations, MLA severance packages, and much more.

results.creator: William Dennis Hendricson
results.description: Who We Are is the story, in a format that is part textbook and part historical novel, of nine families that blended through marriage and other relationships over many centuries into a current 21st century American family, the family of William Dennis Hendricson, that's me, and my wife, Susan Lienau Hendricson. As these nine families evolved over time, they cross paths with the famous and infamous who are highlighted in the stories told in this book:  Willem Frederic George Lodewijk van der Dussen , a founding father of modern genealogy in Europe and first chronicler of Hendricson family history;  Maarten Schenck Van Nydeggan Hendriksz , one of Europe’s most villainous mercenary soldiers and Lambert Barentse Hendriksz , Holland’s most revered naval hero; Peter Stuyvesant , peg-legged soldier-politician leader of the New Amsterdam colony; legendary pirate of the Caribbean Captain Henry Morgan ; ill-fated Miles Morgan , vanished in the Carolina’s a decade before the Lost Colony of Roanoke; Molly Reeve Webster , the Witch of Hadley, catalyst for the Salem Witch Trials; and her nemesis, scientist, public health champion and witchcraft-monger, Cotton Mather ; the mystic idealist, William Penn, whose political concepts guided Jefferson, Franklin and other founding fathers; George Washington , need I say more; Daniel Boone ; legendary frontiersman; Molly Pitcher , the mythical Revolutionary War heroine; General Daniel Morgan , hero of Saratoga and Cowpens in the Revolutionary War; British General Charles Cornwallis , the most renowned Redcoat commander of the Revolutionary War; Moses Black Harris , famed Mountain Man of the American West; Abner Doubleday, Civil War General and rumored founder of baseball; WZ Ripley , a catalyst for 20 th century White Supremacy dogma; Ernie Davis, Heisman Trophy winning college football player; George Preston Marshall, key founder of the National Football League in the U.S. and ardent segregationist; Howard Cosell , America’s leading sports journalist in the 1970s; John Lewis, prominent U.S. Civil Rights leader; and Shirley Povich , Pulitzer prize winning sportswriter, with guest appearances by other notables including Christopher Columbus , on his first approach to the Americas, Roger Maris , U.S. baseball legend, the rock band Blood, Sweat and Tears, voting rights advocate Evelyn T. Butts , rockabilly and country western star Jerry Lee Lewis , and best-selling author of “On Death and Dying,” Elizabeth Kubler-Ross. However, Who We Are does not center on these luminaries; they make cameo appearances, engaging various family members,  past and present, in unique experiences, or serving as catalysts for societal phenomenon that influenced the lives of these individuals. Instead, Who We Are is about people who did the best they could to build a safe, happy and prosperous life for themselves in America beginning in the 17 th century. The individuals in the nine families who first immigrated to America were average folk, working class for the most part, with no royal connections or inherited wealth to prop them up. Two of the original immigrants came from merchant families that previously had accrued wealth in Europe, but through misfortune, inexplicable decisions, and political turmoil, had drifted so far away from prosperity that America was seen as their only recourse. Other original immigrants were from families that had known only the meager existence of tenant farm labor for generations. The first immigrants in two other families arrived on legal missions as young, unmarried men, and elected to seek their fortune in America rather than return to uncertain futures in Europe. Who We Are tells the stories of the people in these nine families before and after their arrival in America. All families have extraordinary stories, and collectively, these stories shape society. William D. Hendricson February 17, 2025

results.title: NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) 20160003380: CubeSat Constellation Cloud Winds(C3Winds) A New Wind Observing System to Study Mesoscale Cloud Dynamics and Processes
results.creator: NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS)
results.description: The CubeSat Constellation Cloud Winds (C3Winds) is a NASA Earth Venture Instrument (EV-I) concept with the primary objective to better understand mesoscale dynamics and their structures in severe weather systems. With potential catastrophic damage and loss of life, strong extratropical and tropical cyclones (ETCs and TCs) have profound three-dimensional impacts on the atmospheric dynamic and thermodynamic structures, producing complex cloud precipitation patterns, strong low-level winds, extensive tropopause folds, and intense stratosphere-troposphere exchange. Employing a compact, stereo IR-visible imaging technique from two formation-flying CubeSats, C3Winds seeks to measure and map high-resolution (2 km) cloud motion vectors (CMVs) and cloud geometric height (CGH) accurately by tracking cloud features within 5-15 min. Complementary to lidar wind observations from space, the high-resolution wind fields from C3Winds will allow detailed investigations on strong low-level wind formation in an occluded ETC development, structural variations of TC inner-core rotation, and impacts of tropopause folding events on tropospheric ozone and air quality. Together with scatterometer ocean surface winds, C3Winds will provide a more comprehensive depiction of atmosphere-boundary-layer dynamics and interactive processes. Built upon mature imaging technologies and long history of stereoscopic remote sensing, C3Winds provides an innovative, cost-effective solution to global wind observations with potential of increased diurnal sampling via CubeSat constellation.

results.creator: Defense Technical Information Center
results.description: This study reviews Sir Henry Morgan's attack on Panama City in 1671. Henry Morgan was successful because he applied combat power correctly. Morgan faced an enemy of superior numbers, yet he was successful. Morgan chose an objective that was thought to be unobtainable, yet he won. Morgan received no formal education in the art of war; he learned from his own experience and the experience of the pirates before him. In his last great exploit Morgan chose the famous city of Panama for his objective. This study shows how Morgan applied the elements of combat power in capturing Panama City, a city never before conquered. This study concludes by showing how the tactics of Henry Morgan are important to the military leader today. Morgan serves as an example of how to apply the elements of combat power. Morgan's use of maneuver is a text book example for young leaders to study today. Perhaps most important is Morgan's example of how leadership is vital to every military operation. The study of Morgan's leadership and how he was able to achieve what others thought could not be done is an example for all leaders.
